findings.finding: The C5 rationale relies on `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log, include_retired=True`. No such parameter exists: the function always reads the full raw log. More importantly, its planner fails closed when a prior SNAPSHOT cites sources that are missing from disk (the 'b636' guard, 'incomplete log'). Once swept events are gone, every swept ticket's SNAPSHOT cites missing sources, so fsck's rebuild-on-stray aborts for those tickets instead of re-inferring provenance. The rebuild also builds `authorship_ledger` only from the raw files present on disk (`_build_authorship_ledger([c.path for c in plan.raw])`), so any rebuild that did run would drop the swept signed events' ledger entries and break the C4 carriage.

findings.checklist_item: Ensure every write path in the streamed engine (:1, :2, and the per-commit SNAPSHOT overrides) honours the drop set.
evidence: Prerequisite: 'Mark :2, the ledger anchor (from :1 ...), is the boundary tree plus inline overrides for every SNAPSHOT whose ledger re-resolves against {boundary: checkpoint}.'

Prerequisite: 'A candidate is any path whose basename contains -SNAPSHOT.json, with or without .retired ... Commit c gets an inline override for every SNAPSHOT path that its diff changed, and for every inherited SNAPSHOT that references a commit mapped after from was written.'
Subject: 'writes the parentless checkpoint as the boundary tree minus that set (D lines after the root M) ... so dropped paths stay dropped and no further rewrite is needed.'
findings.finding: The subject handles the sweep only in the checkpoint. It writes mark :1 as the boundary tree with `D` lines, then states that 'each replayed commit applies only its own changes on top of its rewritten parent, so dropped paths stay dropped and no further rewrite is needed.' The prerequisite's streamed engine has two write paths that can bring dropped paths back. (1) Mark :2, the ledger anchor, is specified as 'the boundary tree plus inline overrides for every SNAPSHOT whose ledger re-resolves'. This matches today's full-tree ledger-anchor commit, so it re-roots the unswept boundary tree on top of :1 and undoes the checkpoint's `D` lines for :2 and every later commit. (2) The engine tracks every SNAPSHOT path in the current tree, including `-SNAPSHOT.json.retired`, and emits inline `M` overrides both for changed SNAPSHOTs and for inherited SNAPSHOTs whose ledger references newly mapped commits. The subject's drop set does not exclude retired SNAPSHOT tombstones, so a swept retired SNAPSHOT can be re-added by such an override in :2 or in a replayed commit.
findings.location: Approach (sweep_retired option; checkpoint D lines; 'no further rewrite is needed') and Scope (drop-set computation, checkpoint D lines)
scenarios: A boundary tree with a signed retired COMMENT that is eligible for the sweep: :1 drops it, but :2 is emitted as the full boundary tree plus overrides, so the COMMENT reappears at :2 and at the tip.

A retired SNAPSHOT folded by a later SNAPSHOT joins the drop set, but its ledger references an above-boundary commit, so the engine emits an inline override for that path in a replayed commit and resurrects it.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the plan so the drop set also applies to mark :2: emit the same `D` lines there, or write :2 as only its overrides on top of :1. Also exclude swept paths from SNAPSHOT tracking and from inline overrides, or exclude retired SNAPSHOTs from the drop set. Add a test showing that a swept path stays absent at :2 and in a commit carrying an inherited-SNAPSHOT override.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Rewrite the C1–C5 bullets with the ADR's own labels and meanings. Say explicitly how ADR C2 (below horizon) follows from boundary eligibility and how ADR C5 (no retained reference to a dropped object) holds. Present CREATE exclusion as a separate rule with its own reason.
evidence: ADR 0106 §C1–C5: 'C2 — Below horizon ... C3 — Remote-anchored ... C5 — No forward dependency. No retained (above-horizon) event or SNAPSHOT references a below-horizon commit_sha that would dangle.'
Plan: 'C2, remote-anchored: ...'; 'C3, stale-clone override: ...'; 'C5, no unfolded dependent: the drop set excludes CREATE events.'
findings.finding: The plan claims to enforce 'ADR 0106's C1–C5 boundary' but gives the labels different meanings from the ADR. ADR C2 is 'below horizon' (the carrying commit's committer-date ≤ now − horizon_days) and ADR C3 is 'remote-anchored'. The plan calls remote-anchoring C2 and calls stale-clone override C3. ADR C5 is 'no retained event or SNAPSHOT references a below-horizon commit_sha that would dangle'. The plan's C5 is a different rule, excluding CREATE events. As a result the plan never states why ADR C2 and ADR C5 hold for the dropped paths. It wrongly suggests CREATE exclusion satisfies C5, and the dependency risk that rule was meant to cover (see the fsck and reader findings) goes unexamined.
findings.location: Approach — the C1–C5 bullet list
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer checks the sweep against ADR C5 and assumes CREATE exclusion satisfies it, so retained readers that depend on the dropped events (fsck sources, metrics) are never checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename: C2 → 'below horizon: follows because every path in the boundary tree was carried by a commit at or before a boundary that has been remote-reachable for N days'; C3 → 'remote-anchored: _remote_horizon_eligible, plus stale-clone override in stale_override.py'; C5 → 'no retained object references a dropped event: <how fsck sources, include_retired readers and ledgers are handled>'. Keep CREATE exclusion as a separate rule.

ADR C5 is 'No forward dependency' (no retained event or SNAPSHOT references a dangling below-horizon commit_sha). The plan's C5 is a new rule that excludes CREATE events. The plan never says it is reinterpreting the contract or why. It also never shows that ADR-C5 (references from retained state to the removed files) or ADR-C2 is satisfied for each dropped path.

findings.suggested_fix: Rename the bullets to match the ADR: C1 folded; C2 below horizon (the path exists in a boundary tree ≤ now − N, which holds by boundary selection); C3 remote-anchored (_remote_horizon_eligible) plus the §5 stale-clone override; C4 ledger carriage; C5 no retained reference to the removed file (cover SNAPSHOT source_event_uuids as read by fsck, and CREATE provenance). findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Require the folding SNAPSHOT for C1/C4 to be a live (non-`.retired`, non-dropped) SNAPSHOT, or prove that later SNAPSHOTs transitively carry `source_event_uuids` and `authorship_ledger`; add a chained-SNAPSHOT fixture.
evidence: "C1, folded: a SNAPSHOT in the same ticket directory of the boundary tree lists the event's uuid"
"C3 ... A clone holding a swept event treats its uuid as known to the remote through the SNAPSHOT's source_event_uuids, so it never re-adds the event."
No rule restricts the folding SNAPSHOT to a non-retired, non-swept SNAPSHOT.
findings.finding: C1 and C4 accept ANY SNAPSHOT in the ticket directory of the boundary tree as the folding SNAPSHOT, including a `.retired` SNAPSHOT. A retired SNAPSHOT that is itself folded by a later SNAPSHOT is a `.retired` path that can meet C1 and join the drop set. When that happens, a swept event's uuid and ledger entry exist only in a SNAPSHOT that was also swept. The C3 argument ('treats its uuid as known to the remote through the SNAPSHOT's source_event_uuids') then has no surviving SNAPSHOT to rely on, unless later SNAPSHOTs transitively carry earlier `source_event_uuids` and `authorship_ledger` entries. The plan does not state or require either.
findings.location: Approach — C1 'a SNAPSHOT in the same ticket directory of the boundary tree lists the event's uuid', C4, and C3
scenarios: Ticket with SNAPSHOT S1 (folds comment C, carries C's ledger entry) later folded by SNAPSHOT S2 into S1.json.retired. Both S1.retired and C.retired meet C1 and are dropped. If S2's source_event_uuids lists only S1's uuid, a stale clone holding C finds no SNAPSHOT naming C and re-adds it. verify-identity also loses C's ledger carriage.
findings.suggested_fix: State that C1/C4 are evaluated only against SNAPSHOT files that remain in the checkpoint (non-retired, or not in the drop set). Compute the drop set as a fixpoint so that no dropped path's only folding evidence is another dropped path. Add an exclusion test where the only SNAPSHOT naming an event is itself a retired SNAPSHOT.

evidence: src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:479 `snapmap = self._snapshot_paths(boundary)`; :583-593 `_snapshot_paths` runs `ls-tree -rz` and keeps SNAPSHOT blobs; :598-621 `_refs` reads and parses each SNAPSHOT blob, caching by oid (it keeps only ledger commit refs, not `source_event_uuids` or ledger `event_uuid`s)
Plan Context: 'origin/tickets holds 77,327 `.retired` files out of 220,989 files in its tip tree' (a measured scale estimate, so this cost concern is evidence-based)
findings.finding: The plan says the engine 'computes a drop set from the boundary tree' without tying it to the boundary scan `_StreamedRewrite` already does. `_write_base` already calls `_snapshot_paths(boundary)`, which runs `ls-tree -rz` on the boundary and reads and caches every SNAPSHOT blob through `ObjectReader`/`_refs`. The plan measured a 220,989-file tip tree, so a separate `ls-tree` plus re-reading every SNAPSHOT blob for C1/C4 would duplicate the engine's most expensive boundary pass.
findings.location: Approach — 'the engine computes a drop set from the boundary tree and writes the parentless checkpoint as the boundary tree minus that set'
scenarios: A real-size dry run does two full boundary `ls-tree` walks and parses every SNAPSHOT blob twice, once for ledger refs and once for sources and ledger uuids.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In _replay/_diff_lines, skip M lines for paths in the drop set, and add a test where a merged side branch forked before the boundary carries a swept path, to show it is not restored.
evidence: reclaim_collapse.py:510-521 — a parent not in old_to_new and not in range maps to self.current_tip; lines come from _diff_lines(self.source_of[first], commit, ...)
reclaim_collapse.py:575-576 — every non-D diff entry becomes an unconditional `M {mode} {oid} path` line
findings.finding: The plan relies on 'each replayed commit applies only its own changes on top of its rewritten parent, so dropped paths stay dropped'. But _replay emits M lines from `diff-tree source_of[first] commit`. When the first parent falls back to current_tip (a parent outside the range, e.g. a side branch forked before the boundary and merged later), that source can lack a `.retired` path the replayed commit's tree has. The diff then emits an M line that puts a swept file back. The plan has no guard that removes drop-set paths from replay M lines.
findings.location: Approach — 'Each replayed commit applies only its own changes ... so dropped paths stay dropped'; AC 1 ('every replayed tree')
scenarios: A clone forks before the boundary, after compaction C1 but before compaction C2 on another clone, and its merge lands after the boundary. The replayed side-branch commit diffs against a source that lacks a C1 `.retired` file and re-adds it.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the computed drop set on _StreamedRewrite and, in _diff_lines, skip any non-D entry whose path is in it (still recording it in `changed`). Add a fixture whose history merges a pre-boundary side branch.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a back-out note and AC: the pre-sweep tip must stay recoverable (named backup ref or retained `original_tip`) until S2 publish plus rollback window closes, update ADR 0106 §3.3/I1 to reflect the non-identical checkpoint, and include a test asserting that restoring the pre-image brings back every swept file with reducer/fsck state intact (mark DATA LOSS RISK).
evidence: Plan: 'writes the parentless checkpoint as the boundary tree minus that set (D lines after the root M)'
ADR 0106 §3.3: 'the parentless checkpoint carrying the boundary's exact tree (identical observable store state)'
ADR 0106 I1: 'No live event file is modified or deleted ... the observable folded state is byte-preserved by the checkpoint tree'
ADR Consequences: blast radius 'mitigated by ... backup refs, and staged rollout (story S2 + rollback design)', yet the plan never mentions how the sweep interacts with these
ABSENCE: no AC or test asserts that, after a back-out, the swept `.retired` files are present again and fsck/reducer/verify-identity agree
findings.finding: The sweep is a one-way deletion, yet the plan states no back-out path and no assertion about state after a rollback. The swept blobs survive only in the pre-collapse history (`CollapseResult.original_tip`, or S2's backup refs). The plan does not require that history to be kept, and it does not warn S2's rollback design that the checkpoint is no longer the boundary's exact tree, a property ADR 0106 §3 step 3 and I1 rely on ('observable folded state is byte-preserved by the checkpoint tree'; 'No live event file is modified or deleted'). DATA LOSS RISK.
findings.location: Approach ('writes the parentless checkpoint as the boundary tree minus that set'); Acceptance Criteria; docs/adr/0106 §3 step 3, §Invariant proof I1
scenarios: S2 publishes a swept baseline, the original shadow/pre-image is discarded, and the swept CREATE-adjacent or signed events cannot be recovered if a C1/C4 misjudgement is found later
A rollback to the pre-image reports success, but clones that already reconverged onto the swept baseline keep a tree without the files

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the replay behaviour when an above-boundary commit writes a drop-set path (either keep dropping it or exclude it from the drop set and the count), and add a test fixture with such a commit.
evidence: Plan: 'Each replayed commit applies only its own changes on top of its rewritten parent, so dropped paths stay dropped'
AC1: 'removed from the checkpoint and every replayed tree'
fsck_restore.restore_deleted_sources writes `name + RETIRED_SUFFIX` files, so above-boundary commits can and do write `.retired` paths
ABSENCE: the Testing list has no fixture in which a post-boundary commit touches a swept path
findings.finding: The plan says 'Each replayed commit applies only its own changes ... so dropped paths stay dropped', and AC1 claims swept files are removed from 'every replayed tree'. But a replayed above-boundary commit that writes a swept path again (an M on a `.retired` path, such as a later rebuild that rewrites retired sources) would silently bring the file back. No test covers it, and `retired_swept` would then over-report.
findings.location: Approach ('dropped paths stay dropped and no further rewrite is needed'); Acceptance Criteria line 1; Testing
scenarios: An above-boundary fsck repair commit modifies or restores a `.retired` file that is in the drop set, and the rewritten tip contains it again while `retired_swept` counts it as swept
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude from the drop set any boundary-tree path that `git diff --name-only <boundary>..<tip>` shows any replayed commit touching, and add a unit test with an above-boundary commit that writes a swept `.retired` path, asserting it is neither counted nor silently resurrected.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either exclude `SNAPSHOT` events (retired or not) from the drop set as a stated rule, or remove dropped paths from the engine's snapmap before the anchor and replay steps, and add an exclusion/regression test with a retired SNAPSHOT folded into a newer one.
evidence: Verified in code: reclaim_collapse.py:479 `snapmap = self._snapshot_paths(boundary)`; :488-492 inline overrides for each snapmap path in the anchor; :523-531 `elif path not in changed: lines.append(f"M {mode} {oid} " ... )` in _replay.
_is_snapshot_candidate matches '-SNAPSHOT.json' with or without '.retired' (silk-unpleasant-jackal plan, Approach step 4).
docs/event-schema.md:54: compaction renames folded files with the `*.retired` suffix, and the S1 fixture explicitly includes 'a retired SNAPSHOT'.
Plan C5 excludes only CREATE; nothing excludes SNAPSHOT.
findings.finding: Retired SNAPSHOTs are not excluded from the drop set. Compaction folds an older SNAPSHOT into a newer one and renames it .retired, so its uuid can sit in the newer SNAPSHOT's source_event_uuids, and an unsigned SNAPSHOT passes C4. The engine, however, builds its SNAPSHOT tracking map from the full boundary tree (`_snapshot_paths(boundary)`) and re-emits those paths. _write_base adds inline overrides for every snapmap path. _replay emits `M <mode> <oid> <path>` for inherited SNAPSHOTs whose ledger references a newly mapped commit. A dropped retired SNAPSHOT therefore comes back in the anchor or in later replayed commits.
findings.location: Approach — drop-set rules C1/C4/C5; src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:_write_base/_replay/_snapshot_paths
scenarios: A ticket compacted twice: SNAPSHOT-1 is retired and listed in SNAPSHOT-2's source_event_uuids, is unsigned, and joins the drop set. It then reappears in the anchor via an inline override, or in a later commit via the inherited-SNAPSHOT M line.
retired_swept counts a file that is still present at the tip.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a rule next to C5: 'the drop set excludes SNAPSHOT events (retired or not)'. That keeps the engine's SNAPSHOT tracking unchanged and also keeps the stale-override and rebuild uuid sources intact.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Tighten C1 so the SNAPSHOT that lists the swept uuid must itself be retained in the swept checkpoint (not in the drop set), and make the reconvergence fixture cover a swept event whose folding SNAPSHOT is retired.
evidence: Verified in code: stale_override.py:129-141 (_unpushed_events) builds `known` from the event filenames in `_tree_paths(git, base, remote)` plus `_snapshot_sources` of the SNAPSHOT paths in that same remote tree.
stale_override.py:19-21: 'An event is unpushed only when its uuid is unknown to the remote tip: absent as a file ... and absent from every remote SNAPSHOT's data.source_event_uuids'.
Plan C1: 'a SNAPSHOT in the same ticket directory of the boundary tree lists the event's uuid' — it does not require that SNAPSHOT to stay in the tip tree.
findings.finding: The C3 claim that a clone 'treats its uuid as known to the remote through the SNAPSHOT's source_event_uuids' holds only when the folding SNAPSHOT is still present in the remote tip tree. stale_override reads source_event_uuids only from SNAPSHOT files listed by `ls-tree` at the remote commit. C1 accepts any SNAPSHOT in the boundary tree, including a retired SNAPSHOT that may itself be swept or later deleted. When the only SNAPSHOT listing a swept uuid is gone at the remote tip, a fresh clone holding that event sees it as unpushed and re-adds it, bringing back the swept file.
findings.location: Approach — 'C1, folded' and 'C3, stale-clone override: already enforced by src/rebar/_store/stale_override.py'
scenarios: A swept COMMENT's uuid is listed only in a retired SNAPSHOT-1, which is also swept (see the retired-SNAPSHOT finding). A fresh clone's reconvergence re-adds the COMMENT as unpushed.
The reconvergence fixture passes only because its folding SNAPSHOT happens to be live.
findings.suggested_fix: Change C1 to: 'a SNAPSHOT in the same ticket directory that is retained in the swept checkpoint (not itself in the drop set) lists the event's uuid in data.source_event_uuids'.
